subject: Commercial + Procurement gate: PO vs card and marketplace vendor registration
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Park <lisa.park@procuredge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 May 2028 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap + procurement questions (PO threshold, marketplace)

Hi Lisa — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and a couple of follow-ups so we can scope the onboarding path with your finance/procurement team:

- Redwood commercial path options we discussed: Hosted API billing (card), Reserved capacity / contract (PO), and Marketplace purchase (vendor registration + marketplace terms).
- For procurement readiness we need clarity on: your standard PO threshold, whether your AP will accept a Redwood marketplace purchase order (if we list there), and any vendor registration slips (W-9, bank details, 1099/Tax).

Can you confirm: what dollar threshold drives a formal PO for ProcureEdge (e.g., > $5k / > $25k)? Also, would marketplace purchases be handled by Procurement or AP directly?

I attached a short procurement checklist that outlines the typical docs we can provide (SOW, W-9, COI, sample invoice). If you prefer, Marissa can run a short intake with your AP team to map the fastest route.

Next steps I propose:
1) You share preferred channel (PO vs card vs marketplace) + PO cadence/timeline.
2) If PO, send any vendor onboarding form and we’ll fill it and return with W-9 + bank remit.
3) If marketplace, confirm which vendor portal and any onboarding windows.

Thanks — I’ll hold off on sending a draft SOW/DocuSign until we have the path confirmed.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-procurement-checklist.pdf
From: Lisa Park <lisa.park@procuredge.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 13 May 2028 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + procurement questions (PO threshold, marketplace)

Rafael — thanks for the summary and the checklist. Helpful. Answers below from our end and copying AP for visibility.

- PO threshold: ProcureEdge requires a PO for any committed spend over $7,500 annually. For pilots under $7,500 we route via corporate card (Purchasing card).
- Marketplace: We prefer marketplace buys only when the vendor is already onboarded in our Vendor Portal. Marketplace purchases still require vendor registration; the portal does the initial checks (tax forms, insurance).
- Vendor onboarding: AP needs the vendor packet you provide plus W-9 and bank remit. If Redwood requires any special contract terms, our Legal will need to review — that can add 5–7 business days.

I attached our vendor onboarding form (filled by vendor) — send back the packet with W-9 and sample invoice and we should be able to expedite.

Lisa Park
Sr. Procurement Manager, ProcureEdge
ap@procuredge.com
attachments: procureedge-vendor-form.pdf
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Park <lisa.park@procuredge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 May 2028 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + procurement questions (PO threshold, marketplace)

Appreciate the clarity, Lisa — that helps a lot. Looping Marissa for AP intake and Aditya for technical attachment info (if the marketplace needs product SKUs or a vendor SKU for the portal).

Marissa / Aditya — two asks for your teams:
1) Marissa: can your team confirm Redwood’s standard PO acceptance flow (Net terms we offer are Net30 for most customers). If ProcureEdge needs Net45 or a negotiated term, flag so I can raise it in pricing.
2) Aditya: ProcureEdge asked whether marketplace purchases would require a vendor SKU or if we can supply a generic Redwood SKU and invoice per usage. Also, they may request a sample invoice format to match their AP ingestion fields.

I’ll attach our W-9 and a sample invoice (one-page stub) once I have the vendor form completed. Goal: get ProcureEdge set up in the portal or confirm PO path by mid-week so we can start a pilot.

Thanks — Rafael
attachments: redwood-w9.pdf, redwood-sample-invoice.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Lisa Park <lisa.park@procuredge.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 May 2028 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + procurement questions (PO threshold, marketplace)

Hi Lisa — welcome, and thanks Rafael for the intro. Quick procurement playbook from our side: 

- PO path: We accept PO with Net30 payment terms by default. For Net45/Net60 requests we need finance approval (please let me know the target term).
- Required docs for AP: completed vendor onboarding form, W-9, certificate of insurance (if required for your vendor class), and the remit instructions. We can also provide a short SOW and a one-line monthly invoice for hosted API usage.
- Marketplace: If ProcureEdge prefers marketplace, we can provide a Redwood vendor SKU and a standardized invoice template. Marketplace onboarding varies by portal (some require product-level SKUs, others accept consolidated monthly billing).

Attached is a condensed vendor packet and a sample one-line invoice we use for usage billing. If you want, I can schedule a 20-min intake with your AP team this week to walk the vendor form and confirm fields so their system can ingest our invoice.

Proposed next steps:
1) Lisa — confirm whether you want us to fill your vendor form and send back W-9 + sample invoice (we can do that today).
2) If PO path, share ProcureEdge’s PO template so we can validate acceptance fields and any required billing contact.
3) If marketplace, tell us the portal name and whether product SKU mapping is required.

If all good, Rafael — I’ll prepare the vendor packet and sample invoice and return it to you and Lisa for upload.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Commercial Lead, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-vendor-packet-condensed.pdf, redwood-one-line-invoice.csv
From: Lisa Park <lisa.park@procuredge.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: ProcureEdge AP <ap@procuredge.com>
Date: Tue, 15 May 2028 09:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + procurement questions (PO threshold, marketplace)

Marissa / Rafael — thanks, that all makes sense. We’d prefer Redwood to fill our vendor form and return with W-9 + sample invoice. I’ve attached a PDF of our PO template for reference (internal). AP will accept Net30.

We can commit to sending a PO for the pilot (expected spend ~ $9k) by next Wednesday (5/22) assuming vendor packet is accepted. Please send the completed packet to ap@procuredge.com and I’ll confirm once it’s in the portal.

Also — if you have a DocuSign link for a pilot SOW or subscription agreement, please send and we’ll sign once Legal confirms (should be within 3–5 business days).

Thanks — Lisa
attachments: procureedge-po-template.pdf
